target.title: fix(openclaw): prevent private state races during publication
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw bridge state publication or recursive cleanup could be redirected, blocked indefinitely, or race with another process when private path ancestry or mutation claims changed concurrently.

## Why This Change Was Made

Private publication ancestry is now created with owner-only permissions, mutations use identity-checked process claims, existing parents and claims are validated by POSIX ownership or Windows ACLs, stale claims recover without unbounded path growth, and cleanup preserves files whose identity changed under it. Directory claims bind both filesystem identity and owner metadata so rapid inode reuse cannot disguise a replaced root. The boundary remains limited to Crabline OpenClaw private-file handling.

## User Impact

Operators can rely on private bridge state publication and cleanup to fail closed under path substitution, concurrent mutation, stale owners, inode reuse, and ownership or ACL drift instead of mutating an untrusted path.

## Evidence

- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm exec vitest run test/openclaw-private-file.test.ts` (`81 passed`, `4 skipped` on macOS); five isolated repeats passed
- Targeted coverage execution: all `81 passed`, `4 skipped` (single-file command exits after tests because repo-wide global coverage thresholds are intentionally unmet)
- `pnpm lint`
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- Codex autoreview with `gpt-5.6-sol` / high reasoning: clean on the final race and inode-reuse fixes
- Linux Crabbox `pnpm verify`: `run_48135b77d181`, `63 passed` test files, `1402 passed`, `8 skipped`; lease auto-released
- GitHub Actions `verify`: success on `b07a902bc382204946f046c4f677d979343b520f`
- Native Windows Crabbox focused suite: pending fresh-host retry after an infrastructure bootstrap timeout
- Public-data scrub: no private paths, hostnames, addresses, or contact data found
- Changelog entry included
